subject: Reconciliation & proposed retention credit split for CloudGrid billing anomaly
messages:
From: Sasha Rivera <sasha@cloudgrid.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudGrid Billing <billing@cloudgrid.io>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Discrepancy on April metering — snapshot and ask

Hi Karthik,

We ran an internal check after our April invoice (inv #CG-0426) and flagged what looks like duplicate metering for two connector jobs between 2026-04-11 and 2026-04-14. Line items are small individually but the aggregated uplift is ~$6,400 USD.

I attached our usage export (usage-audit-q1.csv) — you can see the doubled token counts for project: cg-analytics-prod. Can Redwood help reconcile? At minimum we need either a refund/credit or clear documentation to submit to our procurement.

Two asks: 1) confirm whether this is an ingest-side duplication on Redwood, and 2) proposed remediation (credit memo vs invoice adjustment vs future credit).

Thanks — Sasha
Head of Platforms, CloudGrid
---
Attachment: usage-audit-q1.csv (csv, 82KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Rivera <sasha@cloudgrid.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on April metering — snapshot and ask

Hi Sasha — thanks for the detailed export and the quick heads-up. I dug into the meter logs with our billing ops and we do see an anomalous duplicate write for the connector shard during that window — root cause appears to be a race during a background retry when we rolled a batching change on 2026-04-11.

Proposal from our side: we can apply a two-part remediation to make this simple for CloudGrid while keeping accounting clean:
- Immediate goodwill credit of $3,200 applied to invoice CG-0426 (covers ~50% of the uplift)
- Remaining $3,200 applied as a one-time credit on next invoice (CG-0526) OR, if you prefer, a refundable payment/credit memo that your accounting can book against April.

On VAT handling: since CloudGrid is in the US, we’ll apply the credit net of VAT. If you need a zeroed EU VAT reclass or a credit note with VAT details, loop in billing@cloudgrid and we’ll produce the documentation.

I’ve cc’d Lauren (Sales Ops) and Ben (Finance) to get the credit memo and journal entries started. I’ll also attach a proposed split worksheet and a short incident note for your records.

Next step: can you confirm whether you want the remaining $3,200 applied to the next invoice or issued as a standalone credit memo? If standalone, we’ll route to finance for a formal credit memo and sign-off.

— Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: proposed-credit-allocation.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sasha Rivera <sasha@cloudgrid.io>, CloudGrid Billing <billing@cloudgrid.io>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on April metering — snapshot and ask

Thanks for the detail Karthik/Sasha. Finance reviewed the usage slice and the attached worksheet. We can proceed with the two-part approach Karthik suggested. Operational notes: 

- We will issue a credit for $3,200 against invoice CG-0426 effective the day the credit is posted; the credit will appear as a reduction on your next statement.
- For the remaining $3,200 we need a formal direction from CloudGrid: (A) apply as one-time credit on upcoming invoice CG-0526 (no further signatures needed), or (B) process a credit memo (AR adjustment) requiring Sasha to sign the attached retention-approval.pdf to acknowledge the reconciliation and acceptance of the credit memo terms.
- If you choose a credit memo, export for tax records will include a line for VAT handling; provide billing@cloudgrid your VAT ID if any.

Sasha — if you approve option B (credit memo), please reply with: 
  "We accept the proposed credit memo for $3,200 per the reconciliation attached and authorize Redwood to issue the memo."

I’ll queue the entries once we have your instruction. For transparency, I’ve added a reference to internal ticket BILL-722 so our ledger team links the journal entries to the incident.

Best,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: retention-approval.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

From: Sasha Rivera <sasha@cloudgrid.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudGrid Billing <billing@cloudgrid.io>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on April metering — snapshot and ask

Ben/Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and for owning the issue. CloudGrid would prefer option B: please process the credit memo for the remaining $3,200. We will sign the retention-approval.pdf and return it via DocuSign; once we have the formal memo we can close this on our side.

One small ask on tax: we operate in the US (MA) but have a small EU entity — please include the VAT line item in the memo so our AP team has everything in case we reallocate costs internally. I’ll loop in our AP if you need the VAT ID.

Confirming: you will post the immediate $3,200 as a credit against CG-0426 and then issue a credit memo for $3,200 that we will sign. Thanks — Sasha
---
